_comment: Source metadata stored once and referenced by stable ID. evidenceCategory is the claim each source can actually carry -- it is not a quality score. Nothing here validates PracticeMap's 0.0-10.0 scale, and no source is cited as if it did.

sources.title: Practicing in rhythms and accents
sources.author: Simon Fischer
sources.supports: Complementary dotted rhythms, varying the pattern's starting point, and attending to pitch, sound, timing and ease.
sources.doesNotSupport: Any claim of a measured improvement rate, or that rhythm practice suits every passage.

sources.title: Optimizing Music Learning: Exploring How Blocked and Interleaved Practice Schedules Affect Advanced Performance
sources.author: Carter and Grahn
sources.supports: Limited support for alternating between passages and revisiting them later.
sources.doesNotSupport: An optimal violin practice schedule. Ten advanced clarinettists, with variation across raters.

sources.title: Putting practice under the microscope: The perceived uses and limitations of slow instrumental music practice
sources.author: Emma Allingham and Clemens Wollner
sources.supports: Framing slow practice around a specific purpose, and acknowledging that slow and fast execution can differ.
sources.doesNotSupport: A universally optimal starting tempo or increment. PracticeMap's tempo numbers are app defaults.

sources.title: Classical shifts (Basics)
sources.author: Simon Fischer
sources.supports: Rehearsing a shift through its intermediate note: the old finger slides to the new position before the new finger drops, then the slide is hidden.
sources.doesNotSupport: Which finger a given passage should use; that depends on the edition and the player.

sources.title: Principles of Violin Playing and Teaching
sources.author: Ivan Galamian
sources.supports: Dividing the bow into equal parts for a slurred group; shifting on the old finger; practising with the tempo raised in steps only after control is secure.

sources.title: Splitting the double stop (Basics)
sources.author: Simon Fischer
sources.supports: Practising each voice of a double stop alone with the full bow contact, then tuning the lower voice to the upper before recombining.
sources.doesNotSupport: Fingerings for a particular double-stop passage.

sources.title: String crossing: staying close (Basics)
sources.author: Simon Fischer
sources.supports: Keeping the bow at the level between two strings during repeated crossings and rehearsing the crossing on open strings first.
sources.doesNotSupport: Which string a note should be played on when the part does not say.

sources.title: Backward versus forward chaining in the acquisition of a keyboard skill
sources.author: David W. Ash and Dennis H. Holding
sources.supports: Learning a short sequence by adding one segment at a time (chaining) beat practising the whole sequence at once; forward chaining was slightly better than backward.
sources.doesNotSupport: Results for violin, for long passages, or for experienced players; the task was a short keyboard sequence with novices.

sources.title: It's not how much; it's how: characteristics of practice behavior and retention of performance skills
sources.author: Robert A. Duke, Amy L. Simmons and Carla Davis Cash
sources.publication: Journal of Research in Music Education 56(4):310-321, 2009. doi:10.1177/0022429408328851
sources.supports: The best-retained performances came from practice in which errors were located precisely, corrected immediately, and the corrected spot was repeated until it was stable; total practice time did not predict the ranking.
sources.doesNotSupport: A causal claim: 17 pianists were observed on one passage, nobody was assigned a strategy.

sources.title: Mental practice promotes motor anticipation: evidence from skilled music performance
sources.author: Nicolo F. Bernardi, Alexander Schories, Hans-Christian Jabusch, Barbara Colombo and Eckart Altenmuller
sources.supports: Mentally rehearsing a passage (hearing it and imagining the movements, without playing) improved accuracy and anticipatory movement in skilled pianists, though less than physical practice did.
sources.doesNotSupport: That mental practice replaces playing, or results for violinists.

sources.title: Intonation: testing, relating, comparing (Basics)
sources.author: Simon Fischer
sources.supports: Checking stopped notes against open strings and their harmonics, and tuning by relation to a stable neighbouring note rather than in isolation.
sources.doesNotSupport: An exact intonation system; players choose between equal, just and expressive tuning by context.
